questions.q: In pretraining, where do the labels come from?
options: Human annotators label every sentence
A separate classifier trained on tabular data
The text itself: the target at each position is the next token
The model's own predictions from the previous epoch
questions.explain: Pretraining is self-supervised: the next token in the raw text serves as the label, so no manual labeling is needed.

questions.q: In the toy bigram model, why did the loss stop at about 0.378 instead of reaching zero?
options: The learning rate was too low to ever reach zero
The data is ambiguous, so the best possible loss is the data's own entropy
The vocabulary was too large
Gradient descent cannot minimize cross-entropy
questions.explain: The best a bigram model can do is match the data's conditional frequencies; the entropy floor was 0.375, which training essentially reached.

questions.q: What does perplexity of 1.46 roughly mean for the trained toy model?
options: It is torn between about 1.5 tokens on average
It is wrong 46 percent of the time
It has 1.46 million parameters
It saw each sentence 1.46 times
questions.explain: Perplexity is the exponential of the cross-entropy loss, roughly the effective number of tokens the model is choosing between.

questions.q: After the toy model was fine-tuned on four 'bagel' sentences, its loss on the original corpus rose from 0.378 to 0.736. What does this illustrate?
options: Fine-tuning always improves every behavior
The original corpus was corrupted
The loss function was miscomputed
Tuning on narrow data can cause the model to partly forget earlier behavior
questions.explain: Shifting the model toward new data changed its earlier predictions, so it is important to evaluate old behavior after fine-tuning.

questions.q: What is the reward model trained on in RLHF?
options: Human comparisons of pairs of model answers
Raw web pages with no human input
Only the model's loss on the pretraining corpus
Screenshots of user interfaces
questions.explain: Humans pick the better of two answers; the reward model learns to score preferred answers higher with a pairwise logistic loss.
